cities.d: the capital, sometimes known as "Bandar" or "BSB" for short

x.around: Try to pick up the official map of Brunei Darussalam, as it is easy to read and the public bus lines are easy to follow. The people of Brunei are very helpful to visitors, so don't be surprised after a few minutes of conversation they offer a ride to one of the attractions, as they know how much easier it is to drive there than get there any other way.

hidden.d: Has unfortunately been closed since 2014 undergoing renovations, and as of January 2026 has not reopened.
Huge park close to the city with lots of walking trails and a waterfall.
It was one of the best parks back in 2000s, but these days of glory are faded away long time ago. It got some renovation in 2015 but anyway still some parts of it look abandoned.
This place has many exhibits featuring the different style of houses and lifestyle of those who live on the water village.
Beautiful beach with food stalls, playground and washrooms.

x.intro: Bandar Seri Begawan, also known as BSB or just Bandar, is the capital of Brunei.

must.d: Open to visitors when it is not being used for prayers (opening times are posted by the gate). The mosque is very welcoming and if your clothes aren't considered appropriate you'll be given a robe upon entry.

n.ar: مسجد السلطان عمر علي سيف الدين
n.es: Mezquita del Sultán Omar Ali Saifuddin

must.d: The residential palace of the Sultan. It is usually not possible to enter, yet the huge size of the palace attracts tourists to snap picture in front of the gate.

The water village is a beautiful sight to see hundreds of houses seemingly floating on water. The village, which is the world's biggest settlement on stilts, has been on the river for over one thousand years and was the capital…
Another mosque, that resembles Omar Ali Saifuddin Mosque. Whereas Omar Ali Saifuddin mosque is built to commemorate Sultan Omar, this mosque is to commemorate the current reigning Sultan.

It displays the royal accessories utilised during the coronation, and some reproductions, as well as gifts received by the Sultan from dignitaries and civilians all around the world. Definitely worth checking out.

x.safe: Crime is very uncommon in this tightly controlled small country.

cities.d: gateway town to the unspoilt nature of Temburong

x.around: Bangar is small enough for you to walk around, although it could be quite a hike in the hot sun to get to the administrative offices across the river from the commercial area.
x.intro: For the town in La Union, Philippines, see Bangar (La Union). Bangar is the administrative centre of the Temburong District of Brunei. The quiet small town is relatively isolated as Temburong is separated from the main part of the country (where the capital Bandar Seri Begawan is located) by Sarawak's Limbang district. The town centre is on the downstream banks of the Temburong River.

cities.d: second largest city and border town on the way to Sarawak, Malaysia

hidden.d: A large teapot monument in the middle of the roundabout of Jalan Pandan Lima, Jalan Singa Menteri, Jalan Seri Maharaja and Jalan Setia Diraja.
A mosque in the town with a notable Islamic architecture.

x.intro: Kuala Belait is the second largest city in Brunei. Kuala Belait lies along the Belait River near the South China Sea, west of Seria. Kuala Belait is a river port at the center of an oil field that includes offshore wells. It's very close to the border with Malaysia, and is the first city you'll reach if driving to Brunei from Miri.
Muara is a small port town in Brunei, with the population of about 2,100 (2016).

cities.d: centre for the oil industry, with a dedicated museum and the Billionth Barrel Monument
a small town, located on the banks of Tutong River

x.around: As public transportation such as buses outside Bandar Seri Begawan is not reliable, the way to get around in Tutong is by downloading the ride hailing app Dart.

hidden.d: An old wooden building which used to house the district office and court for Tutong District.

n.en: Old Building of Tutong District Office and Court

hidden.d: A small riverfront promenade along the banks of Tutong River.
The popular beach and recreational area in Tutong District. It is located on the spit created by the meanders of Tutong River on its way to the South China Sea.
A monument to commemorate the 60th birthday of His Majesty Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, the 29th Sultan of Brunei, on 15 July 2006.

x.intro: Tutong is a small town of Tutong District of Brunei. It is located on the banks of Tutong River.

intro: The Sultanate of Brunei is a small but — thanks to natural gas and petroleum resources — very rich country on the island of Borneo in Southeast Asia. Although Brunei is not on most travellers' radar, it is a country of tranquil mosques, pristine jungles, and friendly inhabitants. Its full name is Negara Brunei Darussalam, with Darussalam appropriately meaning "Abode of Peace".

other.d: the first and the only national park established in Brunei, contains unspoilt jungle and is known as the "Green Jewel of Brunei"
